title: Getting started
summary: From download to your first agent at work, in five steps.
text: What you need A Mac with macOS 13 or later, Apple Silicon or Intel. Claude Code or Codex, installed and signed in with your own account. Werkbord drives the agent you already have; it never asks for an API key. A project: any folder tracked by Git. If you can pick one from GitHub, Werkbord copies it to your Mac for you. Not a developer? Werkbord for people who don’t write code walks through the same steps in plainer terms. 1. Install the app Download Werkbord-preview.dmg , open it, and drag Werkbord onto Applications . Open it from there. The first time, it sets itself up in a few seconds and starts a background service. That service is what keeps agents and schedules running after you close the window. This is an unsigned test preview. If macOS says it can’t open Werkbord, try once, then go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway . Step by step . 2. Add a project Setup offers two ways in. Connect GitHub and pick repositories from your list (Werkbord clones them with your own sign-in), or choose a folder on this Mac that is already a Git repository. Each repository becomes a project with its own Board, Calendar, Git view and Runs. Add more later with the + next to Projects in the sidebar. 3. Start a task In your project, choose New task (or press N ). Write what done looks like under What should an agent do? , add any details, pick the agent, and choose Add and start agent . The agent works in its own Git worktree: a separate copy of the repository. Your checkout does not change while it works. Start with something you can check in two minutes, such as a failing test or a small copy change. 4. Watch it, and answer when asked Werkbord 1 2 3 4 1 An agent has a question. The strip names it and takes you straight there. 2 A running agent: a cobalt ring, how long it has worked, and the last thing it did. 3 Needs you: the question is on the card with its answers. One click and it carries on. 4 Finished: the branch and how far ahead it is. Move to Review when you want to read it. The board updates live. You can also answer from the Control Center , the task itself, or your phone . 5. Review and merge Open the finished task to read the change. When you are happy, choose Merge… . Werkbord shows what will happen and checks the repository again the moment you confirm. Werkbord 1 2 3 4 1 Merging happens on this computer only. Nothing is pushed and no pull request changes. 2 What you are about to merge, and whether Git found conflicts. 3 Keep the branch’s commits, or fast-forward only. 4 Only you can press this. An agent finishing never merges. Not right yet? Send it back with new instructions. The next run can pick up the same worktree. Take it further Tour the app Every screen, annotated. Connect your phone Answer questions from anywhere.

title: Installation
summary: Install the Mac app, open it the first time, keep it up to date.
text: Download and install Download Werkbord-preview.dmg (one file for Apple Silicon and Intel, macOS 13 or later). Open it and drag Werkbord onto Applications , then open Werkbord from Applications. Keep the app in Applications. Moving or deleting it later does not break your installation, because the controller it starts lives outside the app. Opening the preview the first time The preview is ad-hoc signed and not notarized by Apple, so macOS refuses it the first time: Open Werkbord once and dismiss the message. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security . Scroll to Security and choose Open Anyway next to the message about Werkbord. Confirm with your password or Touch ID. Signed releases open after a single “downloaded from the Internet” question, like any app. What the first launch sets up The werkbord program in ~/.local/bin . Your data and database in ~/Library/Application Support/werkbord . A login service, so Werkbord is working after you close the window and after you log in again. Closing the window hides the app. ⌘ Q quits the app. Neither stops your controller, your agents or your schedules. Agents Werkbord finds Claude Code and Codex the way your terminal does: the app reads your login shell’s PATH , so agents installed with Homebrew, npm or nvm are found. Sign in through the agent itself first. Settings → Agents shows what was found and links to each agent’s instructions; choose Check again after installing one. Updates The preview has no automatic updater: download the newer release and drag it over the old one. Signed releases update themselves from Werkbord → Check for Updates… , check the update’s signature before installing, and wait while agents are working. To turn off update checks, set "noUpdateCheck": true in config.json . Removing Werkbord Quit the app and delete it from Applications. The background service keeps running until you remove it with werkbord uninstall , which keeps your data. See the command reference .

title: A tour of the app
summary: Every screen, what it is for, and where the buttons that matter are.
text: Control Center Everything that needs you, from every project, in one list. Each item can be answered where it is shown. Werkbord 1 2 3 4 5 1 The count of what waits for you. It follows you everywhere in the sidebar. 2 A question from an agent, with its answers as buttons. 3 Every project at a glance: what needs input, what is running. 4 Agents working right now, with their last line of output. 5 What starts next: scheduled tasks and anything waiting for a slot. Board One project’s tasks in four columns. Moving a card follows the work: Backlog to Doing starts an agent, Review to Done opens the merge confirmation. Werkbord 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 1 The project, its folder and branch. Click the name to switch projects. 2 Jump to any project, section or task. ⌘ K . 3 New task. N . 4 Questions waiting, from any card in this project. 5 The state of every agent, counted. 6 Running: cobalt. 7 Needs you: amber, with the answers on the card. 8 Finished, ready to review. 9 In Review: Merge… or read it first. A task Opens over the board. The activity is the agent’s own account of what it is doing; the bottom of the panel is always the next thing you can do. Werkbord 1 2 3 4 5 1 Where the task is, what it is called, and how it runs: agent, interaction, priority. 2 Stop the agent. The worktree is kept. 3 Activity, details, execution settings, its schedule and every run. 4 What the agent did, as it happened. 5 A decision for you, pinned where you can’t miss it. Calendar The same tasks, in time. Drag a task onto the week, or pick one and click a slot. Scheduled tasks start by themselves, in order, with the window closed. Werkbord 1 2 3 4 5 1 Move by week or jump back to today. 2 The project’s timezone. A schedule means the same thing after travel or a clock change. 3 Day or week. 4 A scheduled task. 5 Tasks without a time yet. Drag one onto the week. Git What the repository looks like right now, and what is waiting on you in it. Werkbord 1 2 3 4 5 1 Health, branches, pull requests, uncommitted changes, worktrees and history. 2 A branch an agent finished, with its commits and where it stands against main. 3 Merge it on this computer, after a fresh check. 4 Repository health: findings you can turn into tasks. They never act on their own. 5 This computer and the remote, side by side. Runs Every agent session, with how long it took and, when the agent reports it, tokens and cost. Werkbord 1 2 3 4 1 The last 24 hours, half an hour per cell, coloured by real runs. 2 Filter by state. 3 A run in progress. 4 Every run: task, agent, runner, state, start, time, tokens and cost. Overview A project’s Control Center: what needs you here, the recent runs, Git at a glance, and what happened today. Werkbord 1 2 1 What needs you in this project. 2 Recent runs. On a phone The same app, laid out for a thumb. Questions come first; the tab bar keeps the rest one tap away. 1 2 Needs you 1 Answer here. 2 Needs you, Board, Calendar, Git and Runs. 1 2 Board 1 One column at a time. 2 New task. 1 A task 1 The decision, at the bottom of the screen. What the colours mean Cobalt Running, and the actions you can take. Amber Needs you: a question, a decision, something waiting. Purple Blocked: the agent stopped rather than guess. Green Finished, ready for review, or done. Red Failed, or high priority.

title: Agents and settings
summary: Choose how a task runs, without repeating your setup.
text: Connect your agents Werkbord finds the Claude Code and Codex already on your Mac. Sign in through the agent itself first; its sign-in stays with it. Settings → Agents shows what was found. If an agent is missing, follow the agent troubleshooting steps . Set useful defaults Execution settings inherit in this order: global, project, task, then a one-run override. The most specific value wins. Set your usual agent once in Settings → Task defaults , and override it only where a project needs something else. Agent default lets the agent choose its own model or reasoning level. The options come from the agents on your machine. Choose how often it asks Ask me when needed The agent pauses at real decisions and puts the question on the card. Autonomous Fewer interruptions. Approvals that need a person still come to you. Stop if blocked The agent stops when it cannot continue without you, and says why. Settings belong to a run Each run records the settings it started with. Changing a project default affects future runs only. To try another agent or model once, use a one-run override instead of changing the task.

title: Tasks and review
summary: Write the task, follow the run, decide what ships.
text: Write a task an agent can finish Say what done looks like, point at the files, and say what to leave alone. One outcome per task, so each can be reviewed and accepted on its own. If something is a judgment call, say “ask me first”. Follow the run The board shows where the work is; the run shows what the agent is doing. A task in Doing can be running, waiting for you, or blocked. Moving a card never starts an agent by accident: only Backlog to Doing does, and it says so as you drag. Werkbord 1 2 3 1 The activity feed: what the agent read, changed and ran. 2 Answer here. Choose an option or write your own reply below it. 3 Stop the agent at any time. Its worktree stays for the next run. Needs you, and blocked Needs you (amber) means the agent asked a question and is waiting. Blocked (purple) means it stopped rather than guess: the card says what it could not decide. Both show their answers on the card, in the Control Center and on your phone. Review before merging Agent work lives on its own branch in its own worktree. When a run finishes, the card says Session finished · ready to review with the branch and how many commits it is ahead. Read the change, run your checks, then Move to Review and Merge… . The merge confirmation re-checks the repository when you confirm and refuses if anything moved. It merges on this computer only; pushing is a separate, confirmed step. Send it back, or hand it on Use Continue with… to start another run on the same worktree, with new instructions or another agent. The next agent sees the existing changes. For shared ownership, claims and reviewer sign-off across people, see Team workflow .

title: Scheduling
summary: Plan work around time, dependencies and how many agents run at once.
text: Schedule a task The Calendar and the Board show the same tasks. Drag a task from Unscheduled onto the week, or set a time in the task’s Schedule section, including from your phone. Werkbord 1 2 3 1 A scheduled task. Drag it to move it. 2 Unscheduled tasks, ready to drag. 3 Schedules use the project’s timezone. The controller starts scheduled work with the window closed. The Mac has to be awake and Werkbord’s service running. Each schedule is one attempt; rearm it to ask for another run. Dependencies A task can wait for other tasks in the same project; its card says Waits for … until they reach Review. Cycles are refused. Finishing a dependency makes the next task eligible; it does not copy the dependency’s code into it, so merge the prerequisite first when the next task needs it. How many agents at once Each project has a concurrency limit from 1 to 16 (1 by default). Running, waiting and blocked runs all hold a slot. Tasks whose files might overlap are run one after the other instead of side by side. If the queue seems stuck, look for a run waiting for your answer before raising the limit. Missed or interrupted runs Choose whether a missed schedule runs late or is skipped after its grace period. An interrupted attempt is not rerun by itself: look at the task, then rearm it when you are ready.

title: Phone access
summary: The same board on your phone, while the work stays on your Mac.
text: Connect your phone Werkbord reaches your phone over Tailscale, a private network between your own devices. It has its own Tailscale node built in, so the Mac needs no extra app, and no Werkbord server sits in between. In Werkbord, open Settings → Phone access , turn it on, and sign in to Tailscale when asked. A free account is enough. Install the Tailscale app on your phone and sign in with the same account. This is the one step Werkbord cannot do for you. Scan the code with your phone’s camera. It opens Werkbord already signed in. Werkbord The code carries your access token. Treat it like a password; it is blurred in this picture for that reason. Put it on your home screen Open the HTTPS address, then use your browser’s Add to Home Screen . With HTTPS and MagicDNS turned on for your tailnet, it installs like an app and can send notifications when an agent asks you something. 1 2 Board 1 Questions waiting, at the top of every page. 2 Needs you, Board, Calendar, Git and Runs. 1 Answering 1 Tap an answer and the agent carries on. Keep it private The phone link includes an access token. Keep screenshots of the code to yourself. Tailscale decides which devices can reach your Mac; Werkbord still asks for the token on every request. Turn phone access off in Settings at any time. If it will not open Check that the Mac is awake, your phone’s Tailscale app is connected to the same account, and Werkbord is running. For setup and certificate problems, see troubleshooting .

title: Additional runners
summary: Send tasks to another machine you own.
text: Pair a runner Use the same Werkbord version on both machines. Install and sign in to the agent on the new machine, with the Git credentials it needs. In Settings → Runners → Add runner , choose the projects it may work on and run the generated werkbord join command on the new machine. Pairing codes expire after five minutes. Bind a repository Each runner works in its own clone. Bind the project to its path on that machine: werkbord runner repo <project-id> /absolute/path/to/repository A binding does not copy your repository or your agent credentials anywhere. Turn on routing deliberately A new runner starts with capacity 1 and automatic routing off. Check its repository and agent before giving it work. Runners and Team A runner runs your own tasks on another of your machines. Werkbord Team coordinates people, each with their own runner. For a shared workspace, see Team setup .

title: Team setup
summary: Create a workspace, invite people, and run the first ticket.
text: Before you start These steps are for people with access to Werkbord Team. Each teammate runs agents on their own machine with individual Werkbord; the Team server only coordinates tickets, reviews and reported repository state. Looking for access? Join the waitlist . 1. Download the Team server Download the werkbord-team archive for your server’s system from the latest Werkbord Team release : macOS, Linux and Windows, for Intel and ARM. Unpack it and put werkbord-team on the server’s PATH . It does not install a service or start anything by itself. 2. Create the workspace werkbord-team workspace create --name "Acme" --owner "Ada" werkbord-team serve Use your own names. Creating the workspace prints the owner’s token and a sign-in link once: store them somewhere safe. The server runs in the foreground at http://127.0.0.1:7430 . Werkbord Team · Acme 1 2 3 4 1 Available to claim, yours, everyone else’s, waiting for your review, and repository warnings. 2 Amber when something waits for you. 3 Workspace, Projects, Board, My Work, Reviews, Repository, Activity. 4 What the team is working on right now. 3. Make it reachable To let teammates in, serve on a wider address with --addr and put it behind HTTPS, or on a private network. A workspace can also have a private network of its own (Team 2.5 and later). Read access and security before sharing the address. 4. Add a project Open Projects , create one, and give it the repository’s address. Each teammate needs their own clone with that Git remote. 5. Invite your teammates From the project’s People & invites , create an invite with a role (member or reviewer) and an expiry, and send it to the person it is for. The code is shown once and can be revoked. Each member gets their own access token; a lost token can be reissued, and the old one stops working. 6. Run the first ticket Install Werkbord on each teammate’s Mac and add the repository with the matching remote. Write a ticket, make it Available, claim it, and choose Open in my runner . Werkbord adds it as a task; you start the agent. Continue with Team workflow .

title: Team workflow
summary: Clear ownership and honest status while everyone works on their own machine.
text: From Backlog to Done Backlog → Available → In Progress → Review → Done Write tickets in Backlog and make them Available when someone can start. Claiming is one guarded operation: two people pressing Claim at once get one owner and one clear answer. Werkbord Team · Acme 1 2 3 4 5 1 The project, your role in it, people and invites. 2 Available: anyone on the project can claim one. 3 Claim it. It becomes yours, with a branch name ready. 4 Your ticket, outlined in cobalt. 5 The pull request, as your Werkbord reported it. Work in your own Werkbord On a ticket you hold, Open in my runner gives you the task text and a handoff to import. Werkbord matches it to your local project by Git remote and creates the task; you start the agent. The Team server never runs agents and never receives your credentials. Werkbord Team · Acme 1 2 3 1 What you may do, depending on your role and whether you hold it. 2 Status, owner, branch and pull request, as reported. 3 Commits reported by the holder’s Werkbord. Review and sign off Submit finished work for review. The diff lives on your Git host; record the merge there, then a reviewer marks the ticket Done. Done is refused while the pull request is open, and a reviewer cannot sign off their own work unless they own the project. Catch collisions early The Repository tab shows what members’ Werkbords reported: branches, pull requests, and what needs attention, worst first. When two active branches change the same file, both owners see it while it is still a conversation. Werkbord Team · Acme 1 2 1 Two branches change the same file. Whoever merges second may have conflicts. 2 Needs attention, pull requests and branches. This is awareness, not action. Team never rebases, merges or resolves anything; that stays in each person’s checkout and on your Git host.

title: Access and security
summary: What is shared, who can act on it, and how it is kept.
text: What Team stores Coordination only: tickets, membership, reviews, and the branch, commits and pull request state that members’ Werkbords report. Never file contents, diffs, paths on anyone’s machine, or credentials. Inputs are validated on the way in: branch names, commit hashes, pull request addresses and relative file paths. Project roles Member Claims tickets and contributes work. Reviewer Reviews and signs off work in the project. Owner Manages the project, its people and its tickets. Project membership decides what a person can see and do. The rules are enforced by the server, not by the page. Tokens and invites Access tokens carry 256 bits of randomness. Give each person their own. Reissuing a token invalidates the old one. Invite codes are shown once, stored only as hashes, and can expire or be revoked. An invite is separate from the member’s own token. Hosting and backups The server listens on this computer only until you give it --addr . Use HTTPS beyond a trusted private network. Set the data directory with WERKBORD_TEAM_DATA_DIR . From Team 2.6, a workspace keeps a full copy of its data on each Workspace Host; --storage single-file keeps it in one SQLite file, team.db . Replication is not a backup: set WERKBORD_TEAM_BACKUP_DIR for scheduled, verified backups. For a single file, back up a running server with SQLite’s .backup command rather than copying the file. Board sync Open consoles receive changes over long polling and reread the current state when they reconnect. In the product’s tests, a change appears on another board in under a second; real networks vary.

title: Troubleshooting
summary: Start with the app, then the service, then the connection that fails.
text: Start here Open Werkbord. If the window cannot reach the controller, it says why and offers Try again , Show details and Open logs . Help → Show Diagnostics… collects the rest. From a terminal, with ~/.local/bin on your PATH : werkbord status werkbord doctor werkbord logs -n 100 Keep tokens and private task details out of anything you share. My agent is missing Check Settings → Agents . If the agent is not found, install it and sign in through it, then choose Check again . If claude --version or codex --version works in your terminal but Werkbord still cannot find it, run werkbord setup from that terminal to refresh the service’s environment, then werkbord restart . Werkbord will not open On the first launch of the preview, use Open Anyway . If the window says another program is using port 7420, quit that program or choose Show details to see which one. My phone cannot connect Keep the Mac awake. Check that phone access is on and that your phone’s Tailscale app is signed in to the same account. Scan a fresh code from Settings → Phone access . If the page loads but home-screen installation or notifications fail, check HTTPS and MagicDNS for your tailnet. A scheduled task is not starting Check that its dependencies are done and a slot is free: waiting and blocked runs still hold one. Look at the missed-run policy and any interrupted attempt, then rearm it. A Team handoff cannot find my project Check that Werkbord is running and that your local project has the same Git remote as the Team project. Importing never starts an agent by itself.

title: Command reference
summary: The werkbord command, for people who like a terminal.
text: The local service The Mac app installs the werkbord command in ~/.local/bin . Add that folder to your PATH to use it. Command Purpose werkbord status Check the installed service. werkbord start Start the service. werkbord stop Stop the service. Refuses while agents are working. werkbord restart Restart the service. werkbord open Open the board in a browser. werkbord open --qr Show a phone sign-in code. werkbord doctor Check setup and dependencies. werkbord logs -n 100 Read recent service logs. werkbord setup Refresh the service’s environment and settings. werkbord update --check Check for an update. werkbord uninstall Remove the service; keep your data. Add a project werkbord project add ~/code/my-app Use the path of a local Git repository. Team server werkbord-team version werkbord-team workspace create --name "Acme" --owner "Ada" werkbord-team serve --addr chooses the listening address. WERKBORD_TEAM_DATA_DIR selects the data directory; WERKBORD_TEAM_LOG_LEVEL and WERKBORD_TEAM_LOG_FORMAT control logging. Read Team setup before serving a workspace to other machines.
